messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode of care described below. A three-character category is one capital letter followed by exactly two digits, for example J44.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Medical Record Number: [REDACTED]

Admission Date: [REDACTED]
Discharge Date: [REDACTED]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient exhibited acute massive hemoptysis upon admission, which was successfully treated through a bronchial arteriography with distal embolization of the left bronchial and phrenic arteries. The patient's bleeding did not recur thereafter, and the outcome was favorable. The patient's respiratory tract sampling was positive for SARS-CoV-2, but there was no evidence of bacterial or viral co-infection.

Laboratory Results:
The patient's CRP was measured at 256 mg/L, lactate dehydrogenase level was low at 237 UI/L, and D-Dimere level was 1228 ng/mL. The anti Xa activity was measured at 20 ng/ml. Serum Aspergillus-specific IgE level was low.

Conclusion:
The patient was discharged from the hospital on D14 with no complications of the vascular interventional procedure. Follow-up care was recommended.

Reply with the three characters only.

text:
Principal diagnosis: massive hemoptysis, with COVID-19 confirmed on respiratory sampling. In ICD-10-AM, hemoptysis is R04.2, and COVID-19 is U07.1. The hemoptysis was the reason for admission and treatment. However, COVID-19 with a respiratory manifestation could be coded as U07.1 as the principal diagnosis, since the hemoptysis is likely due to COVID-19 pneumonia or a related cause. The case report this appears to be based on describes hemoptysis in a COVID-19 patient, with the anti-Xa measurement suggesting anticoagulant use. The bleeding was the focus of care and the treatment given, so the symptom code R04 fits best.

R04
